clue.text: The facts are these: freewheeling stars will break apart defence

indicators.note: the shuffled letters split the defence word into two pieces by sitting inside it

parts.note: in football the backs are the defenders

indicators.note: moving freely without control, so the letters of stars roll into a new order

explanation.surface: A football pundit warns that free-roaming star forwards will tear a defence to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defence' reads as a team's back line in the surface and in the wordplay too, but as the plural backs; brass tacks is the idiom for the plain essentials.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to brass tacks means dealing with the basic realities, the essential facts of a matter.

clue.text: Weapon some strap to their feet

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a high, narrow-heeled shoe

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts look like one picture of an armed person, but they are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a thin dagger and the spiked-heel shoe named after that blade's shape.

clue.text: Get moving to improve method of seduction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an urging cry to hurry up
second meaning: to make progress, as a learner does
third meaning: a flirtatious lure or advance

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one phrasal verb and its noun form sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a shout of encouragement, a verb for progressing, and a noun for an enticing flirtatious approach.

clue.text: Direction provided by leaders of Europe at summit talks

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, taken from each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A diplomatic communique about the course set by European heads of state at a summit meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four compass points, a direction of travel.

clue.text: It preserves well-concealed architectural feature, they say

indicators.note: signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: something deep is well hidden, as a deep secret; a frieze is a decorated band along a wall

explanation.surface: A description of a hidden decorative feature in a building, passed on by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIEZE and FREEZE sound the same, so 'they say' turns the hidden frieze into the freezer.
explanation.definitionFit: A freezer chest keeps food from spoiling by holding it at very low temperature.

clue.text: It is part of nuanced way to explain foreign film

indicators.note: the first word becomes part of the next word by going inside it

parts.note: subtle means finely nuanced

explanation.surface: A film critic praising understatement as the way to make a foreign film understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' at the start looks like a pronoun standing for the answer, but it is the piece to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: Captions translating dialogue let viewers follow a movie in another language.

clue.text: Drake rueful for holding up announcement of discovery

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the words Drake rueful hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Francis Drake, regretful, delays proclaiming what he has found on his voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds AKERUE spanning drAKE RUEful, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes is said to have cried this Greek word, 'I have found it', on making his discovery.

clue.text: Fool horse with backwards look

indicators.note: the look word appears inside the horse word but the wrong way round, so it is turned

parts.note: a colt is a young male horse
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: A silly horse peering behind itself.
explanation.walkthrough: COLT holds OL, which is LO 'backwards'; turning it the right way gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid or clumsy person, an idiot.

clue.text: Reason to restrict availability of alcohol

parts.note: to ration is to limit how much people can have
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone justifying limits on drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying logic or justification for an action.

clue.text: Busy pub talk is essentially quite ordinary

indicators.note: taking the essence, the inner letters, of each of the three words

explanation.surface: The chatter in a crowded pub is mostly humdrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual describes what is normal or customary, nothing out of the common.

clue.text: Quiet one moving east carrying a signal

indicators.note: the rearranged word carries the a within it
in an across entry east is rightwards, so the one shifts a place to the right

parts.note: silent means quiet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A silent soldier advancing east with a message flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving east' shifts the I one place right in SILENT, giving SLIENT; 'carrying' puts A after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective signal means conspicuous or notable, the same as salient, standing out prominently.

clue.text: Case is plain with ivory top inlaid

indicators.note: set into the surface, as decoration inlaid into furniture

parts.note: patent means obvious, plain to see

indicators.note: the top of ivory is its first letter

explanation.surface: Describing a box with a simple body and an ivory lid set into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors refer to a person under their care as a case, i.e. someone being treated.

clue.text: Note skin damage — it's huge, man!

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
tan is sun-darkened skin

explanation.surface: Someone startled by an enormous patch of sunburn.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a giant, one of the colossal Greek deities, so a person of immense size.

clue.text: Initial deal that comes through personal experience

parts.note: first means initial
a hand is the set of cards dealt to a player

explanation.surface: A card player learning the game from the opening deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Firsthand knowledge is gained directly, by witnessing or doing something oneself.

clue.text: Theatrical fellow houses son in apartment

indicators.note: the combined pieces sit inside the apartment word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: the fellow word holds the son word inside it

parts.note: a man is a fellow
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A dramatic man who lets his son stay in his flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested insertions: the son goes into the fellow first, then that goes into the apartment, a flat in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, extravagant behaviour is described as both flamboyant and theatrical.

clue.text: Girl who can cast spells? Spooner says it's dull

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: a witch casts spells
a daughter is a girl, and the word is said as if spelt dater

explanation.surface: A teenage sorceress is told by a clergyman that she is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: WITCH DAUGHTER, with W and D swapped, sounds like DITCH WATER; a girl who casts spells is a witch's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom dull as ditchwater makes stagnant water a byword for tedium.

clue.text: The cool cat a poet made up is absolutely useless

indicators.note: invented or assembled, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a trendy poet who invented a hip cat.
explanation.definitionFit: As useless as a chocolate teapot is a British idiom for something that melts at its only job.

clue.text: One is unlikely to be successful changing our diets

definitions.text: One is unlikely to be successful

indicators.note: altering, so the letters of those words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doubter warns that a change of diet is doomed to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing or elections the outsider is the runner given little chance of winning.

clue.text: Ring round after entrance to find where you can go

indicators.note: the ring and round letters come after the entrance word

parts.note: a portal is a doorway or entrance
O is shaped like a ring
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Directions round a ring road to a gateway.
explanation.walkthrough: A Portaloo is a British brand of portable toilet; 'go' is a coy way of saying use the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name means a portable toilet cabin, the place one may relieve oneself at outdoor events.

clue.text: Club rates redesigned so they are easy to understand

indicators.note: drawn up anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A club revamps its fees to make them simpler for members.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutable, the rarely used opposite of inscrutable, means comprehensible or decipherable.

clue.text: Check on home twice

parts.note: re means on or concerning
in means at home; the clue's twice asks for it a second time

explanation.surface: Looking in on the house twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or spending is to restrain or curb it.

clue.text: I leave country hotel to find wine

indicators.note: the letter I departs from the country name

parts.note: Syria is a country in the Middle East
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller leaving a country inn in search of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrah is a red grape variety and the wine made from it, also called Shiraz.

clue.text: Sweet shop robbed as regulars left on time

indicators.note: in a down clue the time letter is placed on the end of the others
only the letters at regular intervals are left after taking every other one

explanation.surface: A sweet shop was raided just as its regular customers went home on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice served as a dessert, which British English calls a sweet.

clue.text: A municipality confiscating papers causes bitterness

indicators.note: taking and holding the papers, so they go inside

parts.note: a city is a municipality
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A town council seizing documents stirs up resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity is sourness of taste or of temper, a sharp acerbic quality.

clue.text: Act slowly and prevaricate; initially not what this demanded

definitions.text: Act slowly and prevaricate; initially not what this demanded

indicators.note: taking the first letters of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A warning that dawdling and stalling are the opposite of what an urgent request asks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue works both ways: the opening letters spell the answer, and acting slowly is just what an urgent request forbids.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for as soon as possible, an instruction to hurry, not delay.

clue.text: Ulster artist holding lead is just bliss

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

indicators.note: the artist letters hold the lead word between them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
the van is the vanguard, the leading part

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish painter happy to be in the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism nirvana is release from suffering, hence any state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Nobody in Rome raised warning

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means reading from the bottom

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: No one in Rome sounded the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo is the Latin word for no one, the language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Tolerate a new wife moving right out

indicators.note: the right letter goes away from the bride word
the right letter ends up out of the word

parts.note: a bride is a newly married wife

explanation.surface: Putting up with a newlywed who relocates away.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to put up with or endure it.

clue.text: First officer who looks after himself, primarily?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: naval slang for the second in command of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole it looks like a description of a selfish ship's officer; the comma splits it into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is both the executive officer of a warship and an idiom for one's own self-interest.
